purpose: This medication is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is usually prescribed when diet, exercise, or a single diabetes medicine is not enough to keep blood sugar under control. Keeping your blood sugar in a healthy range helps prevent serious complications like kidney, eye, and nerve problems.
how_it_works: This pill combines two medicines that work in different ways to lower your blood sugar. Glyburide tells your pancreas to release more insulin, which helps move sugar out of your blood. Metformin works by reducing the amount of sugar your liver releases and helping your body use insulin more effectively.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, upset stomach, diarrhea, and vomiting, especially when you first start taking it. Low blood sugar (feeling shaky, dizzy, sweaty, or confused) can also happen. Taking it with food can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: A rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis (a buildup of lactic acid in the blood) can occur with metformin — seek emergency help if you feel very weak, have trouble breathing, unusual muscle pain, or stomach discomfort. Tell your doctor before any surgery or imaging test using contrast dye, as you may need to temporarily stop this medication. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, and always carry a fast-acting sugar source in case your blood sugar drops too low.
typical_dosing: The typical starting dose is one tablet (1.25 mg/250 mg) taken once or twice daily with meals. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your blood sugar levels. Never skip meals when taking this medicine, as it can cause your blood sugar to drop too low.
